arxiv-2603-02395:
Luyao Zhang, Sergei Nayakshin, Clement Baruteau, and colleagues propose a new route to planets in tight binaries in this 2026 paper. Dozens of planets orbit one star in close pairs, where discs are cut very small. Classic models form planets inside those stable, truncated discs, which is hard to square. The authors suggest planets and the second star form together instead.

A fast-growing disc fragments far out, making planet-mass objects that drift inward. Continued growth yields one dominant fragment that balloons into the companion star. Many young planets get ejected as free floaters during the turmoil. Simulations show early, heavier planets survive best near the main star. Light planets are usually thrown out. That pattern matches the observed lack of small planets in tight binaries.
arxiv-2603-02495:
Avrim Blum, Keziah Naggita, Matthew Walter, and Jingyan Wang study role model disclosure in social networks in this 2026 paper. People copy role models they observe nearby, without knowing if those models are good or bad. A social planner can reveal some labels, within a tight budget. Revealing a good model encourages copying, while revealing a bad one redirects people.

The planner aims to maximize welfare, the count of people copying good neighbors. Algorithms and hardness results frame what disclosure can achieve. Revealing bad models breaks a key property, submodularity, that makes optimization tractable. A proxy welfare function restores that property and yields near-optimal guarantees. Fairness across groups is also protected within constant factors. Direct connection interventions extend the basic model.
arxiv-2603-02595:
Hongbo Zhao, Qiwei Yu, Andrej Košmrlj, and Sujit Datta study swarms of tiny moving particles that also chase chemical signals. Their 2026 paper builds on a known effect where active particles split into dense and dilute groups on their own. Many real systems add chemotaxis, motion toward or away from a chemical the particles make or use up.

Combining stability analysis, simplified equations, and computer simulations, the authors map when each pattern wins. Chemotaxis can halt or erase the split, or create traveling waves and spirals instead. Their formulas for wave speed and pattern size matched the simulations well. The work gives clear rules for how self-driven, chemical-sensing matter organizes itself.
arxiv-2603-02795:
Ruiyang Zhang, Qianguo Sun, Chao Song, and colleagues turn a multimodal model into an agent that can search the live web. Their 2026 system, VSearcher, handles long multi-step quests that mix text search, image search, and page browsing. Text-only agents search well but cannot see, while multimodal models see but rely on frozen knowledge.

A data pipeline first generates hard multimodal questions and filters them for quality and difficulty. Training then runs in two stages, supervised learning followed by reinforcement learning, to build steady tool use over many turns. The team also built MM-SearchExam, a tough new test that challenges even strong commercial models. Across search benchmarks, VSearcher beat recent rival agents and several commercial systems.
arxiv-2603-02895:
Fu-Chieh Chang, Yu-Hsin Yang, Hung-Ming Huang, and colleagues use formal proof to keep AI-written chip documents honest. Hardware designs in RTL code often lack current specifications, making upkeep and checking slow and error-prone. Language models can draft specifications, but drafts may drift from the design's true intent.

Their framework, SpecLoop, drafts a specification, then rebuilds the circuit from that draft alone. Formal equivalence tools compare the rebuild with the original design, and any mismatch returns as a counterexample for another drafting round. The loop runs until equivalence is proven or progress stalls. Across several models and chip benchmarks, the feedback loop clearly beat one-shot drafting on correctness and robustness.
arxiv-2603-03095:
Sofiane Elguendouze, Erwan Hain, Elena Cabrio, and Serena Villata spot the parts of an argument with a single compact prompt. Argument mining must both find the spans of claims and premises in text and label them, a joint job usually split into pipeline stages. Their 2026 approach hands the whole task to an instruction-tuned language model.

Compact instruction prompts reframe detection as direct text generation, so arguments are marked from raw text with no pre-cut segments. On standard benchmarks, the generative approach beat the best existing systems. The authors note this is among the first full generative treatments of the task. Code and data are openly available. The result suggests careful prompting can replace specialized pipelines for structured language analysis.
arxiv-2603-03295:
Gaia Molinaro and three colleagues ask whether large language models choose goals the way people do. Their 2026 study uses a controlled, open-ended learning task borrowed from cognitive science. Four advanced models take part: GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Centaur, a model trained to imitate human experimental behavior.

People in the task slowly explore and learn, and different people settle on different goals. Most models instead lock onto one early solution and exploit it, a pattern the authors call reward hacking, or they perform poorly. Step-by-step reasoning prompts and persona steering help only a little. The authors warn against swapping human goal selection for current models in personal assistance, science, or policy work.
arxiv-2603-03695:
Minwoo Jung and five colleagues locate robots in forests using a phone-book of trees instead of a mountain of laser data. Forest inventories already catalog stems by compact geometric traits, yet localization methods ignore them and haul around gigabyte point clouds. Their 2026 system, TreeLoc++, works directly on the inventory: a list of tree positions and trunk diameters becomes the whole map.

Coarse retrieval is hardened with a histogram of pairwise tree distances, which encodes the local layout and cuts false matches in look-alike forest. Diameter filtering and a spin-consistency check prune candidates further, and a constrained optimization settles the full six-degree pose. Across twenty-seven sequences in four countries the system localized to centimeter accuracy. Fifteen sessions covering about eight kilometers of trails fit in a map smaller than a single photograph, and data localized two years after the inventory was built.
arxiv-2603-03995: Tian and others propose Spectral Surgery, a training-free refinement of trained LoRA adapters via gradient-guided singular value reweighting. Trained LoRA updates often show an inefficient spectrum, with task effects concentrated in few directions while others stay neutral or harmful. The method decomposes a LoRA update by singular value decomposition, figures component sensitivity from calibration gradients, and reweights singular values within a magnitude limit with directions fixed. Across two 8-billion-setting models and four benchmarks it gives steady gains, adjusting only about 1,000 scalars.
arxiv-2603-04195: Gilanliogullari and others present a unified method for coupled beam optics in accelerators. Many coupled-optics parametrizations differ mainly in gauge choice. Building on this fact, the authors spot descriptors of lattice and beam optics independent of basis and present bounded gauge-invariant coupling settings derived from orthogonal projectors onto eigenmode planes. To obtain smooth position-linked optics functions and steady mode labeling, they present a unifying real method using an SO(2) continuity gauge with Procrustes match. Diagnostics for balance and invariance accompany it.
arxiv-2603-04295: Jouteur and colleagues explore plane geometry for q rationals, numbers Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko introduced for positive real q. They build deformed versions of the Farey triangulation and the modular surface, reading each q rational as a circle like a Ford circle. New Springborn operations act as a quadratic version of Farey addition, picking out homothety centers of circle pairs. The authors use them to derive the q deformed midpoint of Farey neighbours and a new q deformation of Markov numbers.
arxiv-2603-04495: Alonso-Izquierdo and colleagues trace how a massive bound mode deforms vortex geodesics. They study vortex groups of three and four in the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling. Geodesics for symmetric BPS solutions stay unchanged, though motion direction follows a force from changing mode frequency along the path. In generic head on collisions, such as 1 plus 2 vortex or 2 plus 2 vortex cases, trajectories depart strongly from BPS geodesics. That departure heightens chaotic behaviour in forming the final state.
arxiv-2603-04795: Naman and colleagues study adaptive spatial weighting for medical diffusion and segmentation. Lesions occupy small regions against large backgrounds, creating spatial imbalance. LAW assigns per-pixel loss weights in mask-conditioned diffusion, modulating a ratio prior with a delta map. ORDER adds selective two-way skip attention with stage-wise confidence gating to lightweight segmentation. On held-out diffusion sets, LAW lowers FID sharply on Polyps, KiTS19, and BRISC, while improving Polyps mask recovery. Adding generated images to nnUNet training lifts downstream Polyps scores, and ORDER reaches strong results.
arxiv-2603-04995: Luca Cafaro and Farshid Soltani present a loop-quantized version of the Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi dust model in its marginally bound form, describing spherical fall of pressureless dust. The full quantum model is built from non-interacting shells with individual loop dynamics. Single-shell growth is non-singular: collapsing wave packets bounce at Planckian densities and then follow an expanding classical path, resolving the central curvature singularity. The authors compare the theory with Wheeler-DeWitt quantization and note that bounce interference limits the strong theory near the center.
arxiv-2603-05295: Sicheng Fan and colleagues introduce WebChain, the largest open dataset of human-annotated real-world website trajectories, accelerating web-agent research. It holds 31,725 trajectories and 318,000 steps, with visual, structural, and action Triple Alignment. Collection uses a scalable pipeline covering complex, high-value tasks that synthetic methods often miss. The authors propose a Dual Mid-Training recipe decoupling spatial grounding from planning, reaching state-of-the-art WebChainBench and public GUI performance. The work provides data and insights for building and evaluating next-generation web agents.
arxiv-2603-05895: Ghaly introduces LLM-based semantic tagging for UN Security Council resolutions. The goal leverages LLM variability for ensemble data cleaning and semantic tagging. Two metrics, Content Preservation Ratio and Tag Well-Formedness, guard against hallucinations and changes beyond task requirements. These metrics pick the best output across multiple runs of several GPT models. The flagship model led both tasks, while its mini variant reached comparable performance at only 20 percent of the cost. The ensemble selects the optimal cleaned and tagged output across models and runs for challenging texts.
arxiv-2603-06495: Sharma and Trivedi bring COLD-Steer, a training-free framework steering language model activations by copying changes from gradient descent on in-context examples. Their key insight is that fine-tuning effects on a small set can be copied fast at inference without updates. Two ways do this: unit kernel guess tuning them, and finite-difference guess needing two forward passes, no matter the example count. Across tasks and tests, COLD-Steer hits 95 percent power using 50 times fewer samples than the baseline, and backs pluralistic alignment.
arxiv-2603-06595: Zhang and team propose PerContrast, a method gauging each output token's user-specific-information link through causal test, for tailoring language model outputs. Different tokens contribute to tailoring to degrees, with more relevant tokens needing emphasis. Building on that mechanism, the PerCE loss upweights tokens with higher tailoring degrees, gauged during training via a procedure, swapping both. Tests on multiple large language models show PerCE improves tailoring with extra cost, gains over 10 percent and strong carryover.
arxiv-2603-06695: Vincent Ciarcia and Erik Insko ask how long Chutes and Ladders lasts when one die face grows almost certain. They model the game with Markov chains and run Python simulations of random play. They then add choice: after each roll, the player may flip a coin to step ahead on heads or back on tails. The choice rule matters a great deal, and they weigh six distinct non-trivial rules.
arxiv-2603-06795: Anchordoqui and colleagues study quantum mechanics in moduli spaces with a mini-superspace approach, building on Species Quantum Mechanics. From that view, moduli-dependent functions act as operators, and taxonomic relations from the Emergent String Conjecture constrain how far those operators fail to commute. Wave functions show the shape of moduli space matters, giving excited states stuck in the bulks of moduli spaces with positive energy values. With potentials present, states often sit away from classical minima as excited states with positive energy.
arxiv-2603-06995: Biedke and colleagues analyze constraints and quantization in anomalous two-dimensional Thomas-Whitehead gravity. The two-dimensional Polyakov action often appears as the odd part of string theories and fermions coupled to gravity. Gauge freedom makes that action yield zero terms as constraints, even in distinct gauges such as the light-cone and the ADM setup. Two-dimensional gravity theories also arise as actions on coadjoint orbits of the Virasoro algebra, and Thomas-Whitehead gravity extends that action so the key coadjoint element becomes a live field.
arxiv-2603-07095: Zhou and colleagues split the control of a team of legged robots carrying a heavy load together. Central planning captures how robots and load push on each other but scales poorly, while fully separate planning ignores those forces and turns cautious. Their ADMM-based distributed predictive control breaks the global problem into parallel per-robot tasks linked by consensus constraints on the shared load. Each quadruped with a manipulator then plans locally while staying in step with the team.
arxiv-2603-07295: Luthra argues that machine perception should be split into interacting specialist parts, as the cortex is. Single all-in-one models perform well but hide their reasoning and cope poorly when parts must combine in new ways, the paper claims. Her plan makes inference explicit through layered predictive feedback and shared latent spaces. A small trial finds the split yields steadier, more inspectable internal pictures, pointing toward more open machine perception.
arxiv-2603-07695: Correa, Nowak and Pezo study arising spin buildup in open-system altermagnets, focusing on the Edelstein effect. D-wave altermagnets gain new susceptibility components from non-Hermiticity, as do p-wave unconventional magnets, absent in closed twins, shaped by order-parameter symmetry. The leaky nature yields picked gain and loss of specific spin parts, tunable through loss and magnet order. Gain-loss profiles track Néel vector aim, offering a new route to spin control.
arxiv-2603-08295: Agiollo and colleagues present a systematic analysis of attack graph and IDS integration, the first of its kind. Cyber attacks grow harder to catch as high-volume, complex network traffic lets threats stay concealed. While IDSs spot anomalous behavior, attack graphs serve as the main threat model for studying attacker strategies and informing replies. Despite early recognition of the link, the field lacks a common structure. The paper reviews a wide set of prior work and merges the two fields into one framework.
arxiv-2603-08395: Claudon and colleagues realize the Markov Chain Monte Carlo method on a quantum machine in tests. Quantum methods cost greatly less than older ones for certain sampling tasks. QAE offers faster mean values of certain functions given access to the quantum state for that spread. Usually, samples often come from running a Markov chain. The authors use codes of Markov chains to prepare quantum states and run a quantum Markov Chain Monte Carlo routine on Quantinuum hardware. They operate straight on real qubits.
arxiv-2603-08495: Paul Hofman and colleagues offer a cheaper route to honest doubt for machine learning models in high-stakes use. Old credal predictors retrain whole sets of models, which puts them out of reach for large base models and mixed-input systems. Their decalibration trick instead gives each label a band of plausible odds from relative likelihood, with tests showing strong cover and out-of-distribution spotting.
arxiv-2603-08695: Yue Yu and colleagues set new limits on light CP-even scalars using old SN1987A gamma-ray data. Such scalars, born in the supernova core by nucleon braking radiation, can slip out and decay into photons. Seeing no excess glow after the neutrino burst, the team sets new bounds on how strongly the scalar mixes with the Higgs boson.
arxiv-2603-08895: Bilal Ahmad Rather and Hilal Ahmad Ganie study degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, mainly on complete multipartite graphs. They pin down families with three distinct eigenvalues and spot integral matrices. For complete graphs they find the edge-deletion threshold for spectral radius and weighted energy, classify the Randić family fully, and show a leaf-edge addition in stars strictly raises ISI energy.
arxiv-2603-08995: Denis Mamaluy and colleagues argue physics-based first-principles models can co-design efficient AI hardware. Matrix multiplications dominate compute and energy in generative-AI workloads, so per-token energy cuts need joint hardware design spanning chips, wiring, circuits, and system layout. No-fit device and interconnect models close the loop between nanoscale laws and workload metrics, maybe giving tenfold-plus efficiency gains.
arxiv-2603-09095: Kaiser Sun and colleagues study why multimodal models do worse when the same text arrives as an image rather than as tokens. Across seven models and seven benchmarks, the gap swings with font and resolution, and real document pages often show far smaller gaps. Reading thousands of errors, they find the main cause: image input alone makes models reason far less, giving much shorter replies. Fine-tuning on the model's own text-mode traces closes the gap and carries to new tests.
arxiv-2603-09195: Arihant Jain and colleagues introduce P2GNN, a plug-and-play add-on that uses two prototype sets to lift message-passing graph networks. Such networks lean too hard on local context and assume neighbors resemble each other, which hurts under noise. The prototypes act as shared neighbors open to every node, adding global context, and messages aligned to clustered prototypes get a denoising effect. Across eighteen datasets it tops production e-commerce models and ranks first on average on open data.
arxiv-2603-09595: Shreyas Meher guides political scientists through a practical choice in natural language processing: build a domain model, borrow and adapt one, or fine-tune a general model. Using conflict event classification as the test case, Meher fine-tunes ModernBERT on the Global Terrorism Database to create Confli-mBERT. It trails the domain-pretrained ConfliBERT by about four accuracy points overall. The gap concentrates in rare event categories, while on frequent attack types the two models are nearly indistinguishable.
arxiv-2603-10195: Yocam and coauthors cancel hallucination linked signals inside language models in real time, borrowing from adaptive noise cancellation in signal work. Their frame treats those signals as structured interference in the transformer residual stream. Layer wise probes first locate the nodes tied to false text, then a confidence weighted hook tamps them in generation, with no fine tuning or extra passes. Across three model scales the hook lifts truth scores while prose ease and reasoning stay intact.
arxiv-2603-10295: Tae Yun Kim and co-authors give the EPW code a fast GPU port for Wannier interpolation of electron-phonon matrix elements. The design fits the current code and runs across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel hardware. Benchmarks cover silicon, monolayer MoS2, and wide stanene nanoribbons that earlier versions could not handle. The hybrid scheme runs up to 29-fold faster than the old MPI-only route on leadership machines, and scales nearly ideally to thousands of GPU nodes, readying EPW for exascale work.
arxiv-2603-10395: Baoheng Zhu and co-authors present Graph-GRPO, a way to train graph flow models with online feedback toward rewards that can be checked. Aligning such generators with human preferences or task goals is hard, so two ideas carry the work. First, an analytic form for the transition probability replaces Monte Carlo sampling, making rollouts fully differentiable. Second, a refinement step perturbs chosen nodes and edges, then regenerates them for local exploration. On synthetic and molecular tasks the method sets leading scores, beating rival approaches and classic genetic algorithms.
arxiv-2603-10695: Anna Chistyakova and Mikhail Pautov propose RandMark, a random watermarking method for protecting visual foundation models, which are costly to train and often shared under license. A small encoder-decoder network embeds a digital watermark into the internal representation of images from a hold-out set. Because the embedding is random, the watermark's statistics stay detectable in functional copies of the model. Theory and experiments both show low odds of false detection for clean models, and low odds of missing the mark in watermarked ones.
arxiv-2603-11095: Inyong Koo and coauthors improve audio-visual emotion recognition. They tackle a mismatch most systems ignore. Audio and video frames arrive at different rates, and this blurs the timing cues that emotion depends on. Their transformer framework uses a shared multimodal self-attention encoder. Rotary position embeddings align the two token streams in time. A matching loss keeps pairs close in time consistent. On two standard emotion datasets, the design improves over recent baselines. Alignment keeps temporal cues and strengthens fusion.
arxiv-2603-11395: Abdulaziz Alyahya and coauthors help reinforcement learning agents learn tasks without forgetting old ones, replaying memories to a learned world model, not straight to the policy. Model-free buffers devour memory, so ARROW extends a world-model agent with a distribution-matching buffer. It splits into a short-term store for recent experience and a long-term store for task diversity through smart sampling. On structureless and shared-structure task suites, it forgets far less than rival methods at equal buffer size. It keeps forward transfer comparable.
arxiv-2603-11895: Srinivasan and co-authors forecast how well coming surveys can pin down binned modified gravity. They emulate the matter power spectrum for a model where the effective gravity strength and the gravitational slip vary by redshift bin. The emulator matches COLA simulations to better than 1% on the gravity boost. Forecasts pair an LSST-like data set with CMB lensing from the Simons Observatory. Large scale structure probes growth at low redshift, while CMB lensing reaches higher. The best-measured direction is the lensing combination of the two parameters, they find.
arxiv-2603-12195: Pang, Labunets, and Gadyatskaya map how ERP builders and consultants handle privacy. ERP systems hold sensitive data on customers, suppliers, and staff under rules like the GDPR. Work inside one international consultancy firm grounds the study in daily practice. The team probed awareness of privacy-by-design and data minimization in both groups. Thematic analysis through Fogg's Behavioral Model yielded a behavioral model for each group. Those models give managers concrete levers to prompt better privacy behavior in both roles.
arxiv-2603-12295: Panja finds the periodic points of power maps in finite matrix groups and algebras. The map sends each element to a fixed prime power under set conditions on the field size. He counts such points for full matrix algebras and for the general linear group over finite fields. Limit formulas follow as the field grows with a fixed valuation constraint. The same count extends to symplectic and unitary groups, whose limits turn out equal. Regular semisimple elements drive the limiting values in every case studied.
arxiv-2603-12595: Gihoon Kim and Euntai Kim fix a hidden flaw in personal preference learning from human feedback. Standard methods assume one reward for all users, which blocks personalization. Variational Preference Learning adds user-specific latent traits, yet the authors find those traits can collapse and be ignored. Sparse data and strong decoders drive that failure. Their swap-guided method builds fake swap annotators whose mirrored tastes steer the encoder. Tests showed less collapse and better prediction of user choices.
arxiv-2603-12695: Tuğçe Bilen and Ian Akyildiz bring network management into semantic communication for 6G. Such systems aim to keep meaning, not perfect bits, which can save bandwidth. Most past work stops at encoder and decoder design. Their framework adds a reasoning module that scores relevance on a knowledge graph. Routing then favors paths that preserve meaning, and a controller adjusts encoding as conditions change. In ns-3 tests, delivery success rose and distortion fell against baselines.
arxiv-2603-12895: Chantale Lauer and co-authors evaluate a language model copilot for business process modeling with domain experts. Automated checks cover syntax and meaning, yet miss trust, usability, and fit with practice. Five experts tested the BPMN copilot in focus groups and questionnaires. Usability scored as acceptable, while trust ran notably lower. Reliability was the top concern among the group. Output quality and prompting proved hard, and experts wanted deeper clarifying questions from the tool.
arxiv-2603-13095: Oscar Veenema and co-authors model how baryons are pushed out of haloes, and what role feedback and dark energy play. Their analytic model balances gravity, hydrostatic pressure, and cosmic expansion around each halo. It predicts a closure radius where the baryon share meets the cosmic value. Six EAGLE simulation variants, with varied cosmological constant, match the model well. Dark energy proves far from negligible in the process. In high dark energy cases, it becomes the main driver of evacuation.
arxiv-2603-13195: The Euclid Collaboration uses the MAMBO mock galaxy catalogue to predict far-infrared fluxes for Euclid sources. MAMBO builds on the Millennium Simulation and assigns galaxy traits from observed trends. Only the brightest Euclid sources should appear in current far-infrared surveys, the team finds. Stacking shows dust temperature and infrared luminosity rise with redshift, while dust mass stays near constant. The Deep Survey reaches fainter and farther than the Wide Survey, though both lose sources at high redshift.
arxiv-2603-13395: Chiensheng Chiang and co-authors introduce COT-FM, a framework that reshapes flow matching paths. Flow matching models often trace curved paths due to random or batchwise couplings, which raise errors. COT-FM clusters target samples and gives each cluster its own source distribution. Those sources come from reversing pretrained flow matching models, a divide-and-conquer move. The result is more accurate local transport and much straighter vector fields, with no change to model design. It sped sampling and raised quality on 2D, image, and robot tasks.
arxiv-2603-13595: Kurt Butler and co-authors propose a causal framework to handle data shifts in healthcare. Models must work across diverse patient groups and places, yet training data and deployment data often differ. Domain generalization methods fight such shifts, but each rests on its own assumptions and trade-offs. Causality gives a shared language to describe many kinds of shift, no matter the data type. That view shows why models fail to generalize and points to principled ways to prepare for shifts.
arxiv-2603-13695: Nicolas Dickenmann and co-authors steer image models to make EasyRead pictograms for accessibility. EasyRead images are simple, clear pictures that help people with intellectual disabilities, low literacy, or language barriers. Design by hand is slow and costly, yet diffusion models add too much detail and vary in style from seed to seed. Their pipeline fine-tunes a Stable Diffusion model with LoRA adapters on a curated corpus from several pictogram datasets. They also define an EasyRead score to grade quality.
arxiv-2603-13795: Nguyen and co-authors study federated unlearning, where a shared model must forget one client's data. Their framework, FOUL, does the work on the server, so client data stays private and costs stay low. A first stage teaches the model to mark the features tied to the clients who will leave. A second stage then removes that knowledge on the server alone. The team adds a new metric, time-to-forget, and reports that FOUL beats retraining on three datasets.
arxiv-2603-14495: Gyevnár and Kasirzadeh map a split inside responsible AI work. AI safety and AI ethics camps often clash over which risks matter most. The authors name four ways to engage with this divide. Options range from open clash to shared work across the gap. They weigh the gains and costs of each mode. A study of 3,555 papers then maps both research fields. Shared problems exist, they find, but ethics work stresses real harms while safety work stresses future risks.
arxiv-2603-14695: Du, Nam, Liu and Gómez-Bombarelli scale autoregressive models for lattice thermodynamics. Alloy and catalyst design needs the full spread of atomic arrangements. Markov chain sampling slows badly near phase transitions. Autoregressive models learn the distribution directly but fix one generation order. Their any-order models condition on any known subset of sites. Marginalization partners score partial setups in one pass and slash memory. Models trained on small lattices then sample larger ones. Free energy estimates beat multilayer baselines, they report.
arxiv-2603-14995: Manzoni and co-authors study the Zak phase in one-dimensional insulating chains with special symmetries. They ask how much topology this phase can capture across all symmetry classes. Using fibered Hamiltonians, they build symmetric Bloch bases and define a Z2-valued invariant from the phase. They show that in classes with a quaternionic structure, the invariant must vanish. Worked examples on generalized Kitaev chains show the phase keeps only part of the topological picture.
arxiv-2603-15095: Samanta and Bhattyacharya propose a hybrid framework for assigning volunteers to tasks in crowdsourcing platforms. Matching is hard because skills are fine-grained, profiles are messy, and willingness shifts over time. A language model extracts clean skill and preference cues from resumes and task text, but does no assigning. A utility-driven matcher then weighs partial skill coverage and likely participation. Smart contracts enforce the result in a tamper-resistant way. Tests showed about 42 percent better assignment utility, and task coverage rose from 80 percent to 90 percent.
arxiv-2603-15195: Merin shows that gradient transport in real-time recurrent learning is massively redundant, which enables sparse online learning. Full RTRL pushes a Jacobian tensor forward at quartic cost per step. Propagating through a random 6 percent of paths kept about 84 percent of the adaptation skill. Even hostile path choices worked in plain recurrent networks. The Jacobian is full rank but near-isotropic, so small subsets still point the right way. Sparse propagation also proved more stable on chaotic dynamics and on real primate neural data.
arxiv-2603-15395: Dey and Fring use Bohmian mechanics to probe a two-dimensional ghost Hamiltonian tied to the Pais-Uhlenbeck model. With Gaussian wave packets, they derive the guidance equations plus the center, width, and quantum potential paths. These tools sort the motion into bounded, near-classical, spiral, and runaway regimes. They then compare a pair of classically equal Hamiltonians. Both give the same classical paths but distinct Bohmian paths and quantum potentials. Classical equivalence, they conclude, need not survive in Bohmian quantum dynamics.
arxiv-2603-15795: Du and Peng link central L-function derivatives to heights of Heegner cycles. Gross-Zagier type formulas tie such derivatives to arithmetic geometry. Earlier work covered newforms in set weights. The pair proves an intersection formula for general cusp forms. The derivative equals a global height pairing of higher Heegner cycles. They also study modularity of the cycle generating series. A weak form of the modularity claim is proved. The full claim reduces to a vanishing claim with supporting evidence.
arxiv-2603-16095: Xue and co-authors predict a time-domain Efimov effect in an expanding condensate. Spatial Efimov physics rests on scale invariance of three-body states. A time twin breaks time-shift symmetry but keeps scale symmetry. Their analog universe is a flat condensate that coasts outward. Phonon rules stay fixed under time rescaling. Output grows by power law or log-periodic waves. Log-periodic ringing marks the Efimov signature in time. Both map to sub- and super-horizon cosmic modes. Density spectra in rigs can test the claims.
arxiv-2603-16395: Xu and co-authors test whether cosmic censorship can fail in a scalar field model. The conjecture says singularities should hide behind event horizons. Their model couples scalar fields to gravity and light with a fractional term. Some black holes there grow negative energy density near the horizon. Simulations of shaken versions show curvature rising fast nearby. The horizon structure weakens as the coupling grows. The trend hints at a naked singularity forming.
arxiv-2603-16595: Rahimian builds a baseline framework for uplink links aided by smart reflectors. Mobile users connect directly and through an intelligent reflecting surface. The surface steers phases with finite-bit settings. Focusing adapts by inverse-rate priority weights per user. Channels are handed out in sequence, guided by energy detection. The math stays physics-based, with a two-hop path-loss model. Exact chi-square thresholds guide the detector. A MATLAB run serves as the worked example.
arxiv-2603-16695: Hibi, Kara, and Vien study the independence polynomial of a finite simple graph. They focus on its value at x = -1 and its symmetry. The polynomial also links to the h-polynomial of the edge ideal. For big star graphs they pin down when the value is 0, 1, or -1. Only one big star has a symmetric polynomial, they show. Leaf-grafting formulas extend the results to caterpillar graphs. Symmetric cases for cochordal graphs are fully classified.
arxiv-2603-17095: Queiroz, Siqueira, and Yaguna test whether multi component dark matter can explain the Galactic Center GeV excess. A single particle species struggles to match the excess's spectral shape. The authors scan sectors with two and three distinct species, with exclusive and mixed annihilation channels. Model choice is judged with the Akaike Information Criterion, which penalizes extra complexity. They find the data favor two components, each annihilating into a single final state. Preferred solutions pair a light species with a heavy one.
arxiv-2603-17295: Zhang and co-authors present a two stage framework for story visualization that keeps characters and style consistent across frames. Story images must track an evolving narrative while holding identity and look steady. Their first tool, Group-Shared Attention, lets attention layers share information across samples without loss. Their second tool uses Direct Preference Optimization to align outputs with human taste and narrative standards. On the ViStoryBench benchmark, they report gains of 10 points in character identity and 18.7 in style consistency.
arxiv-2603-17595: Mohapatra and Pal study fractional revival and pretty good state transfer on graphs. They work with adjacency, Laplacian, and signless Laplacian matrices. Under set conditions, fractional revival survives graph complementation, they show. A link between a graph and its double cover then drives the main result. They fully characterize pretty good plus state transfer in cycles and their complements. Weighted paths with potential get matching results.
arxiv-2603-17995: Dutt and co-authors propose LoST, a way to tokenize 3D shapes by level of meaning, not detail. Early tokens decode into whole, plausible shapes with the main traits. Later tokens add fine shape and meaning details for each case. A new loss, RIDA, aligns shape latents with DINO semantic features. LoST beats past detail-based tokenizers on reconstruction and needs far fewer tokens for generation.
arxiv-2603-18495: Kim and co-authors present NeSyCR, a framework that adapts robot code from video demos to new settings. Sight and physics gaps between demo and real use break direct code reuse. Demos first become symbolic paths that hold the core steps of the task. What-if states then show where the new setting clashes with those steps. A checked search over the state space writes fixed code, and task success rose 31.14% over Statler.
arxiv-2604-00195: Drissi introduces Lévy-Flows, normalizing flows swapping the Gaussian base for Variance Gamma and Normal-Inverse Gaussian distributions. These heavy-tailed bases keep exact likelihood evaluation and efficient sampling, and theory shows the tail index survives asymptotically linear transforms. Identity-tail spline flows preserve the base tail shape exactly outside the transform region. On Standard and Poor's 500 returns and others, Variance Gamma flows cut negative log-likelihood by 69 percent against Gaussian flows. They reach exact 95 percent VaR calibration, while Normal-Inverse Gaussian flows give the best Expected Shortfall estimates.
arxiv-2604-00295: Patel and five colleagues derive multi-dimensional conservation laws for stimulated Raman scattering and Brillouin backscattering in a density slope, under paraxial rays. A Lagrangian density gives the wave equations for both cases without damping, and Noether's theorem turns its patterns into action and energy laws. These reduce to Manley-Rowe relations in one dimension, plus frequency and wavenumber matching rules. Extra action patterns yield laws for orbital angular momentum and energy and momentum parts from frequency and wavenumber shifts.
arxiv-2604-00695: Andersson and colleagues compare spin-phonon action in iron phosphide-based magnetocaloric materials. Magnetic cooling offers a green way to cut cooling-device energy use, but devices need abundant matter, barring rare earths. Iron phosphide-based compounds show cooling promise. The team studies iron phosphide and a compound with magnet tests, neutron beams, and theory, aiming to grasp the shift behind the cooling effect. Crystal data show the 3g iron site drives the magnetic transition in iron phosphide, while the 3f site adds nothing at the shift point.
arxiv-2604-00795: Speziali and colleagues propose PG-IPRO, a method for planning city routes that fit each person's access needs and tastes. Users give feedback on a route, saying which goal should shrink further and which can ease off, guiding the search step by step. Because the system never computes the full set of possibly best routes, it runs faster and keeps waiting times short. It works best in early rounds.
arxiv-2604-00995: Guo and Xia study the multidimensional Chinese remainder theorem, which rebuilds integer vectors from remainders modulo integer matrices for signal processing. Since matrix moduli do not commute, the extension brings theoretical and algorithmic hurdles. They show that under equal determinant constraints, non-diagonal matrices do not widen the dynamic range but give more balanced, better-conditioned sampling patterns and lattices with longer shortest vectors, raising error robustness. They develop a multi-stage robust framework with a simple matrix condition, beating single-stage robust versions on error tolerance.
arxiv-2604-01195:
Nandan Thakur and co-authors present ORBIT in 2026, a system for training search agents. Search agents join language models with web search for hard questions. Building training data for deep research tasks remains costly and hard.

Such tasks involve multi-step retrieval and reasoning over many sources. Human annotation is expensive, and other routes carry cumbersome prerequisites, they note. ORBIT aims at scalable and verifiable data generation on a tight budget. Its title promises exactly that economy with checks on quality. Cheaper, verified training data could widen who can build research agents. The paper speaks to teams training agents without large annotation budgets. It treats data generation itself as the bottleneck to solve.
arxiv-2604-01395: Weeger and colleagues offer a blueprint for on-premises retrieval-augmented generation systems in firms. Strict data rules bar many firms from cloud services, yet most blueprints focus on cloud setups and lack firm-grade parts. Their blueprint gives an end-to-end reference architecture in the 4+1 view model and a reference application for on-premises deployment. It also gives best practices for tooling, development and CI/CD pipelines, all on GitHub. Case studies and expert interviews with industry partners will assess its practical benefits.
arxiv-2604-01895: Bartolucci, Jevnikar, Wei and Wu prove a sharp spectral bound for a superlinear free-boundary problem from plasma physics. The equation's constraint forces a nonlocal eigenvalue problem, so its first eigenvalue obeys no general Faber-Krahn-style isoperimetric rule. Working carefully on balls in every dimension from two upward, the authors show that first eigenvalue stays positive throughout. They also draw out what the result means for uniqueness in the related Emden equation.
arxiv-2604-02195: Qiu and Wu study continuity of weighted Dirac spectra under changes in the weight. They show the two sided weighted spectrum varies continuously as the weight deforms within a uniformly elliptic class. For smooth families of weights they add a quantitative Lipschitz estimate for the full spectrum in the arsinh metric, built on a weighted Hellmann Feynman variational identity. The result ties spectral stability to weight regularity in a sharp, explicit form.
arxiv-2604-02395: Jana and Roy study illusion removal on one way social networks with red and blue nodes. A node suffers illusion when red out neighbors beat blue ones despite more blue. Ending it with the fewest flips proves NP hard even on grids, and W[2] hard by recolor count on two part DAGs. No fast algorithm exists on DAGs unless P equals NP, and none follows from size plus cycle distance. Yet fast answers exist for outerplanar networks, outward grids, trees and cycles, plus fast methods by treewidth and deficiency.
arxiv-2604-02495: Ruškuc and Yayi introduce relational depth for finite semigroups whose J-classes form a chain. The notion measures how far down the ideal structure one must go to define the semigroup by generators and relations. They compute the exact value for every ideal in three central monoids: the full transformation monoid, the symmetric inverse monoid, and the partial transformation monoid.
arxiv-2604-02895: Sengupta argues that black hole mass can be replaced by a topological charge in a spacetime without matter or curvature singularity. Static bubbles are the case studied. His bubble spacetimes weave together degenerate and nondegenerate metric phases of first-order gravity in vacuum. For a static bubble, the boundary surface joining the phases carries a universal topological number. It coincides with the photon sphere of a standard black hole, while a boundary at the event horizon proves topologically trivial. The result reframes mass as topology.
arxiv-2604-02995: Silva introduces a penalised Saito functional for line arrangements, scoring determinants against the polynomial. It ranges from 0 to 1, hitting 0 exactly for free cases. It is upper semicontinuous and tends to a binary freeness test as its value grows. Numerical estimates guide replacement searches, and each arrangement is then certified by Saito's rule. The certified database holds 6,146 entries with distinct prints up to size 28, including 3,012 with gap at least 2 and extremes at gap 7.
arxiv-2604-03295: Wu and colleagues compare scaling multi-agent language-model systems by adding agents versus by accumulating experience over time. Their LLMA-Mem framework gives teams flexible memory topologies for reusing experience, and tests on MultiAgentBench show it improves long-horizon results while cutting cost. Larger teams do not always win: smaller teams can beat bigger ones when memory supports experience reuse well.
arxiv-2604-03495: Propp and colleagues show that a single photon spread over modes can prepare many qubits from afar at once. That speeds up distant state setup for quantum networks. A photon shared across at least two modes holds up to log base two of the mode count in qubits. It works through a reflection scheme. For many-qubit setup, success rates stay high despite fast-growing numbers of time modes, since only one photon must be sent and detected.
arxiv-2604-03595: Shui and colleagues propose ProtoGuard-SL, a server-side defense for split learning that exploits class-conditional representation match in the code space. Benign codes within a class show stable meaning match, while poisoned codes disrupt that structure. A two-stage framework builds robust class models and turns codes into a prototype-match form. It filters odd codes with a class-based, distribution-free conformal rule.
arxiv-2604-03995: Tianle Chen and Deepti Ghadiyaram studied cross-modal typographic attacks on audio-visual reasoning, a risk as multimodal models enter safety-critical use. Small changes to speech and on-screen text shifted model reasoning, lifting attack success on WorldSense for Gemini 3.7 Flash from 9.53 percent to 43.41 percent. The team mapped how attack traits shape overall reasoning across tasks from content moderation to robot task choice. Fine-tuning as a defense cut Qwen2.5-Omni-7B attack success markedly.
arxiv-2604-04195: Gabriel Diaz Ramos and team introduced the Non-Parametric Gaussian Copula, a synthesis method for private, stable educational data. Older deep generators often warp marginal distributions and drift under repeated regeneration, losing distributional support. Their method anchors on observed spreads while tracking links through a copula, adds differential privacy at both spread and link levels, and treats missing data as its own state. Tested on five benchmark sets, it stayed stable across regeneration cycles with competitive downstream performance at far lower compute cost.
arxiv-2604-04295: Yoo, Xu and Cao build a cheaper, more reliable way to check patent claims. Lightweight checkers miss long legal links, while full model checks cost four to five times more at million-claim scale. Their ACE framework routes by error type. A tuned encoder scores each claim across legal error types, and uncertain claims pass to an expert model reasoning under a patent-thought schema tied to 35 U.S.C. standards. The schema cuts delay by 42 percent, and ACE beats a supervised 70-billion-parameter model while cutting costs by 78 percent.
arxiv-2604-04495: Fowler offers a category-theoretic frame for Greimasian narrative programs, making their compositional structure precise. Building on the actantial model as a schema, he refines the actant typology and derives Set-valued instances for role-indexed parts. Programs sit in a schema using monads on Set. The List monad gives Kleisli semantics for list-valued actant setups, while the Maybe monad encodes links between programs. In this framework, programs act as morphism makers, joined through wiring diagrams, so a tale path becomes a whole morphism.
arxiv-2604-04695: Gowtham Sidharth M and Sanjit Das study the shadow cast by a spinning Bardeen black hole in asymptotic-safe gravity. Null geodesics are analyzed with the Hamilton-Jacobi splitting method to derive shadow measures. An increase in both the safety parameter and the spin parameter shrinks the seen shadow size and increases shadow distortion. The monopole charge of the black hole plays a key role in the shadow profile. The team also computes the energy emission rate for varying values of the safety parameter.
arxiv-2604-04795: Chávez and Li study decision problems where a fixed risk measure judges total cost. Their cases cover Markov decision processes and stochastic optimal control. They add extra state variables that let dynamic programming equations work on the enlarged space. That device lets them examine how many samples each problem class needs. The same device yields a general framework for risk-averse problems built from divergence-based robust models, with new results for common divergence functions.
arxiv-2604-04895: Jarczewski and three colleagues propose Agentic-FL, a shift from fixed federated-learning protocols to language-model agents that orchestrate distributed training. Server-side agents use contextual reasoning to reduce selection bias among uneven clients. Client-side agents guard privacy budgets and adapt model size to local hardware. The authors frame this as a move toward negotiated, decentralized collaboration and future incentive-based model markets. They warn that hallucinations and security risks must be managed for resilient systems.
arxiv-2604-05095: Giovanetti shows that early-time solutions to the Hubble tension usually increase the preferred baryon density. That shift puts these models in tension with Big Bang Nucleosynthesis, since measurements of primordial deuterium constrain baryon density at the percent level. Current work is already in tension with the BBN value of baryon density. Including a likelihood term for deuterium deters two sample models from reaching a high Hubble constant. Early-time solutions thus face a generic baryon-density problem.
arxiv-2604-05295: Li and six colleagues analyze 2018 SOHO observations comparing blob properties in active region and quiet streamers. Active region blobs occur about twice as often as quiet blobs. Active blobs have higher initial velocities and higher accelerations, but lower heights than quiet blobs. Initial velocities and heights correlate weakly positively in both groups. Accelerations and heights correlate negatively in active blobs but positively in quiet blobs. Results suggest higher activity at a streamer's base causes more dynamic blobs and affects solar wind structures there.
arxiv-2604-05895: Kuba and Levy work out full asymptotic expansions for a set of integrals as n grows, tying rates to Nielsen's generalized polylogarithms. When q equals -1, growth runs over multiple zeta values that boil down to plain ones. A mirror rule forces flip-flop cases to plain zeta polynomials, checked for Euler, Bernoulli, Genocchi, and Hermite sets.
arxiv-2604-06095: Jelodar and colleagues' 2026 paper presents LLM4CodeRE, a domain-tuned language-model setup for two-way code reverse engineering. It turns assembly into source and source into assembly in one model. Old methods lean on generic pretraining and adapt poorly to malware, a gap the setup targets. Two fine-tuning plans shape the model: a Multi-Adapter approach for task syntax and meaning, and a Seq2Seq Unified approach using task prefixes. Tests show it beats old decompilation tools and general-purpose code models with two-way generalization.
arxiv-2604-06195: Hintsanen reframes language-model hallucination as misclassification at the output edge, where model-made completions ship as if backed by evidence. The fix pairs refusal prompts with a gate that scores support shortfall from self-consistency, paraphrase stability, and citation coverage, blocking output past a threshold. Across 50 items, five regimes, and three models, neither tool alone suffices: refusal prompts over-abstain on answerable items, while the gate misses confident confabulation under mixed evidence. Combined, they reach high accuracy with low hallucination, though some over-abstention remains.
arxiv-2604-06395: Freddi and three colleagues tackle tuning to the edge of chaos in spiking reservoir computing, energy-lean time handling. It brings the robustness interval, settings keeping scores above thresholds. Leaky Integrate-and-Fire tests cover static MNIST and moving Ball Trajectories. Robustness-interval width shrinks with link density and firing threshold. Some density-threshold pairs preserve the mean-field critical point, showing iso-score sheets. Erdős-Rényi tests show patterns hold beyond small-world shapes. The critical point lands inside high-score regions, a robust starting point.
arxiv-2604-06495: Narayanaswamy and three colleagues improve sparse autoencoder strength with masked regularization, swapping tokens at random during training to disrupt co-occurrence. Sparse autoencoders project language-model signals onto sparse latent spaces for mechanistic interpretability, yet sparsity alone poorly signals it, and goals yield brittle codes. Feature absorption is key: general traits are folded into narrow ones through co-occurrence, harming interpretability despite faithful rebuilds. Poor out-of-sample results show weakness from vague goals. Masking lifts strength, cutting absorption, aiding probing, and closing the out-of-sample gap.
arxiv-2604-06595: Gan and six colleagues report the first tilt measurement for a double M dwarf system, TOI-5375, using the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. The primary star's spin lines up closely with its low-mass companion's orbit, which lasts under two days, suggesting the pair formed aligned or was tidally realigned. Comparing giants, brown dwarfs, and binaries, they find aligned orbits favor cooler hosts and wider separations. No clear link shows up between tilt and orbital eccentricity in any group.
arxiv-2604-06695: Xu and six colleagues diagnose why long reasoning traces go astray. Their Step-Saliency tool pools attention-gradient scores into step-to-step maps across the question, thinking, and summary stages. Two failures recur. In shallow lock-in, early layers fixate on the current step and neglect earlier context. In deep decay, deep layers lose grip on thinking and the summary attends mostly to itself. Their StepFlow intervention repairs shallow patterns and adds a small deep-layer residual, lifting accuracy on math, science, and coding tasks without retraining.
arxiv-2604-06895: Cui and four colleagues model Markov chains with memory on hypergraphs through tensors. Many systems depend on group structures and memory, not just pairwise links. Their unified tensor framework introduces an even-order paired tensor linking folded and unfolded dynamics and characterizes steady states and convergence. A chain with memory can be approximated by a low-dimensional nonlinear tensor system, with full system analysis provided. Applied to hypergraph random walks, where memory arises naturally from hyperedge structure, the tools open higher-order networks with time-dependent effects to analysis.
arxiv-2604-07095: Lyngbaek and Kristensen-McLachlan ask whether multilingual word vectors truly hold a tongue free sense of learner skill. They train plain and curved probes on hidden states from seven embedding models to guess CEFR skill levels from learner texts across nine sets and seven tongues. Inside one set, probes score well and beat a baseline built on surface text traits, with middle layers doing best. Across sets, scores fall apart for every probe type and model size, and stray probes drift toward guessing all levels alike.
arxiv-2604-07195: Zhou asks whether three principles alone can pin down tree-level scattering amplitudes in particle physics. He rebuilds the single-soft rules for Yang-Mills amplitudes and the double-soft rules for nonlinear sigma model amplitudes from locality, unitarity, and newly found hidden zeros. Earlier work shows full amplitudes follow from those soft rules. He therefore concludes that the three principles fully determine the tree-level amplitudes in both theories.
arxiv-2604-07595: Penaroza introduces reasoning graphs that let language model agents keep chains of thought across runs. Each candidate keeps structured edges recording past verdicts for that exact item. A second retrieval graph feeds a planner that drops candidates rejected time and again. Together they make a ROZA graph, a self-improving loop with a frozen base model. On MuSiQue and HotpotQA, accuracy rises 10.6 points over vanilla RAG at 50 percent or higher coverage, with 46 percent lower cost and latency.
arxiv-2604-07795: Choi and four colleagues bend three-dimensional meshes so they take on the geometric style of a reference image. Typical generative models offer only timid variations, but this method deforms shapes boldly. Pretrained diffusion models read the image style in abstract form. A coarse-to-fine pipeline then bends the mesh while keeping its topology and part-level meaning. An approximate variational autoencoder supplies gradients from rendered views, and results carry expressive poses and silhouettes from the pictured assets.
arxiv-2604-08395: Tran and Nguyen show that existing backdoor attacks on vision language models are far easier to spot than claimed, once defenses from vision only and text only models are adapted. They then introduce Phantasia, an attack whose poisoned replies shift with each input's meaning instead of repeating a fixed pattern. Across varied model designs it kept top attack success while holding up under defenses and keeping normal performance intact.
arxiv-2604-08595: Meshkov offers temperature controlled verdict aggregation for judging AI systems, letting strictness fit the domain. His TCVA method scores verdicts on five levels and combines them with a generalized power mean. A temperature knob sets rigor from strict to lenient: low values suit safety critical use, high values suit chat. On human rated benchmarks it matches RAGAS on faithfulness and beats DeepEval, with no extra model calls when temperature changes.
arxiv-2604-08895: Bansal and colleagues present FolpsD, a model of galaxy clustering that joins small-scale power spectrum data with large-scale bispectrum measurements. Extending the FOLPS code, they pair a one-loop effective-field-theory power spectrum with a tree-level bispectrum in a tripolar spherical harmonic basis. A line-of-sight damping factor adds extra small-scale detail. For a dark energy model with varying equation of state, the joint analysis tightens constraints by 15 percent on one dark-energy parameter and 21 percent on the other.
arxiv-2604-09395: Choudhury, Rathod, and Yadav present insights from farmer-managed local solar watering, looking at how farmers maintain grid-linked schemes that pay them to feed energy to the grid. Solar watering is used more and more in rural regions, yet spread rollout makes upkeep hard for farmers. Formal watching steps and apps exist but often fall short in practice. Farmers face troubles but also devise tactics, including using WhatsApp to share daily output data with peers and compare results across sites to spot faults.
arxiv-2604-09595: Xin and four colleagues name a trap in post-training compression. Shrunken models often run no faster, because ragged tensor shapes clash with the graphics-processor stack. They trace this dimensional misalignment across framework, library, and hardware levels. A compressed Llama-3-8B with 15 percent fewer parameters runs no faster than baseline, since 95 percent of its dimensions misalign. Their GAC wrapper re-selects hardware-aligned dimensions under the same parameter budget, restoring full alignment and winning back up to 1.5 times speedup with quality preserved.
arxiv-2604-10095: Jiang and six colleagues ask whether low-rank adaptation subspaces for 3D foundation models line up with distinct data variations. The variations include texture, geometry, camera motion, and lighting. They generate synthetic sets with controlled variation, fine-tune one adapter per set, and extract the subspace tied to each variation. Those subspaces turn out nearly disentangled. Combining them yields a smaller adapter subspace that fine-tunes more efficiently with better accuracy downstream. Although derived purely from synthetic data, it transfers to real data sets.
arxiv-2604-10195: Tremblay, Bergeron, and Beauchamp study He I line shapes used to analyze DB white dwarfs. They analyze every DB white dwarf in Sloan Digital Sky Survey Data Release 17, in photometry and spectra. Their study weighs sampling, Doppler broadening, line dissolution, spread by neutral particles, and 3D flow effects. Above all, they compare the semi-analytical Stark profiles widely used for DB white dwarfs against recent Stark-broadened results from simulations.
arxiv-2604-10295: Pan and nine colleagues present Icicle, a framework for continuous file system metadata indexing and monitoring. Traditional tools like find and du fail at billions of files, while external indexers stay batch-oriented. Icicle keeps a unified, current view of file system state, with snapshot and event ingestion from Lustre and Storage Scale. Built on Kafka and Flink, it ingests events into two indexes for file discovery and summaries by user, group, and directory. Tests on production-scale data show large throughput gains, with tunable consistency, latency, and freshness.
arxiv-2604-10395: Okamura disproves a guess about sums and peaks of half normal random draws. Arnold and Villasenor had claimed a link between the sum and the largest value in such samples. His proof breaks that claim for draws that are free and share one half normal law. The same line of proof also reaches a wider class of broad gamma laws. The short note thus closes the guess and hands later work a more general tool.
arxiv-2604-10495: Goloburda and six colleagues split language model doubt by its source. Most scores blend all doubt into one number, hiding what kind of trouble lurks. Their new data set tags each case by source: knowledge gaps, output wobble, or input vagueness. Methods that shine on knowledge gaps alone stumble or mislead on the other kinds. The lesson is plain: honest uncertainty tools must name the source, not just the size.
arxiv-2604-10595: Rapoport, Behar, and Desjacques test how well the IllustrisTNG simulation reproduces cool gas around galaxies, traced by low-ionization metal lines in quasar spectra. They compute magnesium and iron absorption under collision-only ionization and under an added ultraviolet background, then compare the patterns with HIRES, UVES, SDSS, and DESI observations. The background model matches magnesium counts up to modest line strengths, but the simulation undercounts strong systems and misses their rise toward earlier times.
arxiv-2604-10695: Zhang and five colleagues address audio-visual questions when one input channel goes missing, a common failure that sharply degrades current systems. The usual fix fills gaps by generation, capturing shared patterns but missing channel-specific knowledge and risking hallucination. Their R2ScP framework instead recovers missing knowledge by retrieval through shared semantic embeddings. A purification step strips noise from retrieved data, and two-stage training models relations between sources. Tests show large gains in accuracy and robustness when inputs are incomplete.
arxiv-2604-10895: Bian, Chollet, and Guha propose SocialLDG, a multi-task frame teaching robots to read social interaction by modeling the live link between users' hidden states and visible actions. Both spring from one socio-cognitive process and shape each other over time. A language model supplies word priors for six tasks, while dynamic graph learning tracks how task links shift over time. SocialLDG tops prior results on two public human-robot sets, learns new tasks smoothly without catastrophic forgetting, and reveals how interactions unfold and how states and actions steer choice.
arxiv-2604-10995: Plank and six colleagues explore an epidemic model with complex contagion, where uptake rises nonlinearly with behaving contacts. Simple models assume a linear rise, but social contagion often works in a curved way. Key parameters include the basic reproduction number, the behavioural effect on transmission, and uptake speed versus abandonment. In some regions, the model shows multiple disease-free and endemic states, so complex contagion can prevent diseases from becoming endemic.
arxiv-2604-11395: Pei and four colleagues improve video-based heart rate estimation under facial motion with two plug-and-play modules. An angle-guided module quantifies region-of-interest to camera angles to refine motion-affected signals and capture global motion. A graph-signal denoising module jointly models signals within and across face regions to suppress motion artifacts. Compatible with reflection-model methods and validated on three public datasets, joint use cuts mean absolute error by an average of 20.38 percent over baseline, with ablations confirming each module's contribution.
arxiv-2604-11795: Douglas and nine colleagues build ordered atom arrays, spread out in space with gaps smaller than a light wave, that emit light jointly in a new way. In flat two-dimensional arrays they see strong super- and subradiant glow, images that resolve single sites, and spatial patterns that grow as joint decay turns into a strongly linked many-body process. Superradiance grows with size and shows revivals, acting ferromagnetic, while subradiance acts antiferromagnetic.
arxiv-2604-12195: Yu, Kaushik, and Thompson ask which features of interaction data help learning agents improve, comparing traces of expert-novice interaction with expert action alone. In a spatial navigation task with synthetic data, models trained on pedagogical interaction proved more robust across scenarios than models trained only on expert demonstrations. The key gain came from representing agents as epistemically distinct, which yielded expert-like behavior even when expert conduct was rarely seen.
arxiv-2604-12295: Kaijie Yang and four colleagues study excitons in twisted layers of molybdenum ditelluride. An exciton binds an electron to a missing electron, called a hole. They show such pairs can carry a large electric dipole. The dipole twists in a helix across momentum space, driven by band curvature. An applied field flips the pair from tightly bound to spread out. It also reverses the twist, offering a way to steer many-particle effects.
arxiv-2604-12395: Sricharan Raghavan-Chitra, Arghadip Koner, and Joel Yuen-Zhou test when plain optics can describe light spectra of molecule clusters. Plain methods use only each molecule's linear response as quantum input. The team starts from a full quantum model of the whole cluster. With infinitely many identical, fully linked molecules, plain methods become exact. A series in inverse molecule count adds finite-size quantum effects. Those effects show up as Raman-like jumps of single molecules. A two-molecule test case shows the results in action.
arxiv-2604-12495: Louis-Brahim Beaufort extends geodesic flow results to flows with magnets. First, he studies the magnetic ray transform and proves a tensor tomography result. Second, he treats ergodicity of the magnetic frame flow under pinching. Prior work guides the approach. New Pestov identities power the proofs. They extend and improve prior work. The framework adapts covariant differentiation, torsion, curvature, and Jacobi fields to magnets. His tensor extends a proposed sectional curvature.
arxiv-2604-12695: Yutaro Nagae and two colleagues study Andreev reflection at a junction with a superconductor. The V2O magnet has spin-split Fermi surfaces that are nearly one-dimensional. A small model captures sublattice freedom. Varied boundary conditions still yield robust specular reflection with distinct spin polarization. A multi-lead setup detects the reflection through distant conductance. Such magnets offer a platform for spin-resolved Cooper pair splitting. Such splitting is key to energy-entangled electron pairs.
arxiv-2604-12795: Javier Minguillón and two colleagues pin down Sobolev regularity for pointwise convergence of Schrödinger solutions. Solutions follow tangential curves toward their initial data. For Hölder curves with parameter below one half, maximal estimates govern the work. The model family uses power curves with exponents across space. Critical regularity is the larger of two terms: one from the curve parameter, one from dimension. The result gives the sharp threshold for almost everywhere convergence along such curves.
arxiv-2604-12995: Bao and 11 colleagues tackle a gap in how language models grasp public policy. Their PolicyBench gathers 21,000 cases spanning United States and Chinese policy, testing factual recall, conceptual reasoning, and problem solving in lifelike scenarios. They also build PolicyMoE, a mixture-of-experts model with separate experts for each thinking level, which proves strongest on structured reasoning tasks.
arxiv-2604-13195: Moghni and five colleagues study red geysers, massive quiet galaxies with weak bi-symmetric ionized outflows, tracing cool neutral gas through sodium absorption in 140 galaxies. About 70 percent of the cool gas flows inward at a median 47 kilometers per second. Absorption appears more often in red geysers than in matched controls, at 63 percent against 40 percent. Radio-detected systems host inflowing reservoirs about 7 times larger, and environmentally affected galaxies about 2.7 times larger, pointing to interactions replenishing gas that feeds central black hole activity.
arxiv-2604-13295: Li and Mossel examine what t-SNE, a popular tool for reducing dimensions and visualizing data, necessarily loses. Every dimension-reduction method can discard important features, and the authors build a mathematical framework to pin down that loss for t-SNE specifically. Across several scenarios they prove results showing how key features of the data vanish when t-SNE compresses it. The work gives a rigorous basis for judging when t-SNE pictures can mislead and which structures they cannot be trusted to preserve.
arxiv-2604-13395: Li, Zhao, and Huai ask how sure we can be about answers from large reasoning models. Old tools give no guarantee for a full chain plus its answer. Conformal prediction makes uncertainty sets with no distribution assumption, but old versions miss the link between trace and answer. The authors fix that link, give guarantees for the joint structure, and use Shapley values to pick training examples and key steps that keep those guarantees.
arxiv-2604-13695: Suhail, Anand, and Sethi introduce Med-CAM, a framework that explains medical image decisions with minimal, sharp evidence maps. Most medical AI acts as a black box, offering little insight into why it reached a diagnosis. Med-CAM builds a segmentation network from scratch to highlight only the evidence critical to the model's decision, for seen and unseen images alike. Unlike fuzzy Grad-CAM regions, its maps faithfully replicate the prediction and stay consistent with model activations, aiding clinicians in pathology and radiology.
arxiv-2604-13995: Alam and colleagues work out image and video orientation, which way a picture faces, from depth patterns in natural scenes. Their method reads the depth spread across image quadrants. It refines fit with a depth-gradient match and mirror checks. The hybrid approach suits VR, AR, self-driving, and watching. Tests show it beats older methods across varied scenes.
arxiv-2604-14295: Yu and Chubukov show that a repulsive Hubbard-type interaction, cut off at finite range, can select the subleading topologically nontrivial gap solution in a singular-interaction model. In systems studied so far the trivial gap holds the lowest energy, but in some range the added term favors the nontrivial one. A minimal model displays the switch, which must pass through a middle phase with topology-induced time-reversal breaking. The work thus ties unusual pairing to multiple topologically distinct gap functions from a singular frequency-dependent interaction.
arxiv-2604-14595: Tint argues that recent diversity progress in natural language processing clusters disproportionately around fairness, leaving other areas behind. Incentives, biases, and barriers, he says, push marginalized researchers out of non-fairness fields or into fairness work. Drawing on a demographic study of researchers by subfield, he offers recommendations for making every NLP area more inclusive and equitable. Breaking self-reinforcing feedback loops and easing geographical and linguistic barriers to participation stand out among his proposals.
arxiv-2604-14995: Gupta and Short study recurrence time for finite quantum systems. Recurrence time means the time for all time-evolved states to return close to their initial configuration, with at least one state deviating significantly meanwhile. For finite-dimensional systems evolving unitarily, they bound recurrence time for continuous and discrete time using Dirichlet's approximation theorem. They relate bounding recurrence time to approximating differences of real numbers by rationals, and prove a mathematical result on the latter giving tighter bounds.
arxiv-2604-15095: Misko, Starkova, and Lagoudakis show that KPZ scaling can arise in a smooth, continuous polariton fluid, not only in patterned lattices. They trap a quasi-one-dimensional condensate with light and run large stochastic simulations with lab-realistic settings. The phase correlations follow scaling powers near three tenths in time and just under one half in space, with Tracy-Widom fluctuation statistics. The result roots KPZ behavior in the continuous fluid itself, with natural noise smoothing.
arxiv-2604-15195: Altas and others revisit static tidal perturbations of relativistic stars, fixing two points in the quadrupolar setup. They derive the regular-center expansion of the inner master function and correct its subleading value against common prior work. They also derive the master equation for a Schwarzschild-de Sitter background, taking the flat case to a two-horizon shape. Model runs for polytropic stars show the correction touches only subleading initial data, leaving Love numbers unchanged.
arxiv-2604-15395: Psiris and seven colleagues review foundation models in robotics, tracing five research phases from early language and vision models to multi-sensory generalization and real deployment. Their taxonomy spans model types, architectures, learning paradigms, knowledge stages, tasks, and application domains, with comparative critique at each step. Dataset notes plus a ranked look at open problems and next steps rounds out the survey.
arxiv-2604-15695: Ganguly, Jonnalagadda, Chintamani, and Ananth show team play breaks fast when mates learn together, since each move shakes the other's next move. Even a best-for-all team deal falls apart for good once mate noise tops a key line. Risk-shy payoff guards make it worse: fear hits the risky team move harder than quitting. The fix guards the learning-step wobble itself, not payoffs. A guard widens the safe zone; the Price of Paranoia gauges the good that learning can win back.
arxiv-2604-15895: Venkateswaran and 10 colleagues present a digital predistortion framework for flux control of tunable superconducting qubits. Fast flux pulses drive two-qubit gates, but flaws in control gear, stray parts, and chip response warp the pulses and hurt gate fidelity. Their method measures then fixes these distortions with impulse-response filters. Tests on a flux-tunable quantum processor show the fixed signal tracks the ideal closely, within under one percent, allowing quick self-tuning of flux channels.
arxiv-2604-16595: Crnogorčević searches supernovae for GeV gamma emission in Fermi-LAT data. Magnetar and circumstellar models predict such emission once ejecta turn transparent to high photons. They find no emission, capping gamma-to-optical efficiency below a thousandth. That is two orders of magnitude below predictions for magnetar nebulae. Studies show fewer than 0.7 percent of them can exceed ten to the minus two. SN egm shows excess near four sigma favoring a magnetar origin. Nearby SN bsz non-detection disfavors efficiency, and an excess from SN jlc needs monitoring.
arxiv-2604-16695: Bernardi and colleagues build a lithium niobate receiver for time-bin quantum links. Time-bin light states matter for quantum tech, and chip-scale handling enables networks. The device switches time-bin states with bandwidth over 30 GHz and supports projective reads over 1 GHz. It proves entanglement, breaking Bell's rule by 38 deviations and over 95 percent visibility. In a fiber key sharing test, it holds secure key rates over 25 kbits per second across 12 hours. Active switching removes post-pick, closing a safety loophole and easing sensor timing demands.
arxiv-2604-16795: Dai and Wang study long-time behavior of a branching-diffusion flow tied to a drifted Schrödinger operator. They prove fast convergence rates for the total mass and map its near-steady distribution. The proof uses a novel spectral transformation and heat kernel estimates for Sch boxes with open fields. The result is new even in one line, beating recent work on the topic.
arxiv-2604-16895: Hovad and Engsig-Karup track a single particle in video with an autoencoder that locates it as a heatmap peak. A physics module then forces the resulting path to obey known dynamics. Their Physics-Informed Landmark Loss enforces that consistency without labels, and its supervised variant reaches sub-pixel accuracy, finer than one pixel, under clean and noisy conditions.
arxiv-2604-16995: Huo and eleven colleagues tackle a narrowing effect in RL training for reasoning models, where probability mass piles onto a few high-reward paths and exploration dries up. Standard training lifts single-answer success while starving multi-answer performance. Their SPS approach alternates plain reinforcement learning with inverse reinforcement learning. It treats sampled rollouts as demonstrations to reshape the path distribution, improving multi-answer scores across five reasoning benchmarks and exposing an empirical ceiling on them.
arxiv-2604-17095: Couey hunts for verified mono-monostatic bodies, convex uniform bodies with exactly one stable resting position under gravity. Sloan's analytical gömböc shape, long unproven in published form, fails his test: its height landscape shows 4 to 11 local minima. Extending Sloan's phase function with Fourier terms and optimizing by differential evolution, he builds three verified bodies with an equilibrium count score of one across merge thresholds from 0.5 percent to 10 percent, with uses from IMU housings to seed pods and buoys.
arxiv-2604-17295: Ding, Zhang, Dai, Wang, and colleagues sort time-series reasoning into four levels of rising difficulty. Time-series reasoning means reading patterns in data over time. They build HiTSR, a set of 83,000 examples with checked step-by-step reasoning traces.
